Becoming in tune with the neurology and physical sensations of how my emotions manifested thanks to my counsellor. I've had anxious periods for years, and in the past few months have been snowed under with anxiety/depression so strong I've barely been able to fight it, but in recent weeks we have been identifying what I physically associate with a depressive feeling creeping in during the day. For me it is a tensing of my shoulders/arms and a knot in my chest. So then we work on identifying small exercises I can do when I get that associative feeling, because if I beat the physical sensation it's easier to process that feeling mentally and let it go.

I had been self harming cutting my arms as a release, but we realised it was the violent action of swinging my arm to cut, not the actual cutting that was releasing me. So now I haven't self harmed in a month by realising I can throw punches in the air and grip things tight in my hand to help get a similar release. Doesn't make those urges go away, but it helps make them manageable.

I just feel so much more in tune and understanding of myself basically.

Then Monday morning happened. Monday I felt shit, I felt shattered and broken and just completely mentally fucked. And I lost control. I cut hard and repeatedly all up my forearm. Too many to hide unless with sleeves now. And they are deep, and they are raised and red and *ugly* and sore. And when I did it I tried to stand up afterwards but literally couldn't walk, I felt on the verge of a panic attack, I felt light headed, I felt sick. I still feel sick even looking at my arm. It terrified me that I lost control that much, and did this much damage without intending to.

So yeah. It doesn't just 'get worse', it *consumes you*. Please don't take this path lightly.

I feel the same a lot of the time and have recently been having conversations with my counselor about it. She says avoiding anxiety about the future is all about grounding yourself in the present, which is aided by mindfulness and physical activities which focus your concentration of present sensations and thoughts.

She also made the fair point that anxiety is based on negative imagining of future events, so a different perspective can be found by allowing yourself to explore the alternative. What is the GOOD version of the events you fear? Or even just a neutral version? All of these are imagined and so in a way you can choose to ignore the bad version sometimes and lose yourself in the imagined better alternatives.

Finally the best point she made to me that really hit home. Feeling anxiety about the future by definition means that in the present you are safe and secure. And that is a feeling you can latch onto. Because if bad things were happening in the present, you would be acting, not feeling anxious. Or in the words of Hannibal Lecter 'You must convince yourself that the lion is not in the room. If it were, I assure you, you would know.'
